Im Ergebnis darf davon ausgegangen werden, dass das Bauwerk in einem erhaltungswürdigen Zustand ist, wofür jedoch umfangreiche Sanierungsmaßnahmen durchgeführt werden müssen. Neben der Sanierung des bestehenden wurde auch der Bau eines neuen Nachklärbeckens auf der Fläche des bestehenden Schönungsteichs untersucht und technisch-wirtschaftlich bewertet. Auf Basis einer Wirtschaftlichkeits- und der Nutzwertanalyse wurde dem Neubau eines Nachklärbeckens unter Berücksichtigung der Betriebssicherheit und Zukunftsfähigkeit eine Vorteilhaftigkeit eingeräumt. title: Germany – Real estate services – Verkaufsberatungs-/Maklerdienstleistungen für den NDR Standort Landesfunkhaus Kiel
description: Der Norddeutsche Rundfunk (NDR) ist die Rundfunkanstalt der norddeutschen Länder. Schleswig- Holstein, Hamburg, Niedersachsen und Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. Als Anstalt des öffentlichen Rechts ist der NDR an die einschlägigen Haushalts- und Vergaberichtlinien gebunden. Aufgrund aktueller Entwicklungen im öffentlich-rechtlichen Rundfunk ist der NDR bestrebt, seinen Immobilienbestand auf betriebsnotwendige Gebäude zu begrenzen. In Folge von betrieblichen Veränderungen durch die Einführung einer Multikanal-Strategie (Crossmediales Funkhaus), der Einführung von Desk-Sharing und damit eingehender Flächenreduzierung sowie festgestellter baulicher Sanierungsbedarfe wurde entschieden, dass eine Anpassung des Immobilienbestands in Kiel sinnvoll ist. Hierbei handelt es sich um die Liegenschaft des heutigen Landesfunkhauses belegen am Schloßplatz 3 / Wall 62 - 72 / Flämische Straße 19 - 25 mit einer Grundstücksgröße von insgesamt ca. 4.400 m2 und einer Gesamtnutzfläche von rd. 10.000 oberirdischer BGF. Die Rahmenbedingungen des NDR als Anstalt öffentlichen Rechts müssen in diesen anstehenden Verkaufsprozessen/-verfahren jederzeit berücksichtigt werden. Der NDR beabsichtigt, einen Dienstleister zu beauftragen, ein strukturiertes Bieterverfahren durchzuführen, um die Liegenschaft bis zum 31.12.2028 zu veräußern. Hierzu werden qualifizierte Verkaufsberatungs- /Maklerunternehmen gesucht, die sämtliche Leistungen rund um die Vorbereitung, Marktansprache, Vermarktung, Interessentenkommunikation und die Begleitung des Verkaufsprozesses bis zum Abschluss des Eigentumsübergangs übernehmen. Die zu vergebenden Leistungen sind so durchzuführen, dass der Verkaufsprozess zielgerichtet, professionell, transparent und erfolgreich abgewickelt wird.

title: Germany – Petroleum products, fuel, electricity and other sources of energy – Gemeinde Ostseebad Karlshagen / Beschaffung von Wärme-Contracting
description: Die Gemeinde Karlshagen (Auftraggeberin) unterhält mehrere Gebäude. Für die aufgelisteten Gebäude werden mit dieser Ausschreibung die Bieter aufgefordert ein Angebot für die Wärmelieferung als Gesamtkonzept abzugeben. Die ausgeschriebene Leistung ist ein Energielieferleistung für städtische Wohnungsbauten sowie für die Schule, Kindertagesstätte und die Turnhalle des Ostseebads Karlshagen. Die Wärmelieferung beginnt in der Heizperiode 2027/2028, spätestens ab dem 01.01.2028. Die Vertragslaufzeit soll 10 Jahre mit einer einmaligen Verlängerungsoption von 5 Jahren betragen. Die Lage sowie die Energiebedarfe der Gebäude können dieser Leistungsbeschreibung sowie den Vergabeunterlagen entnommen werden. Die in Anlage C.4 gelisteten Abnehmerinnen (verbindlicher Ausschreibungsumfang) bilden die Grundlage der Angebotskalkulationen / dieser Ausschreibung. Mit dem Angebot ist ein schlüssiges technisches und wirtschaftliches Gesamtkonzept vorzulegen. Weitere Anforderungen an die einzureichenden Unterlagen ergeben sich aus den Vergabeunterlagen.

title: Netherlands – Social work services with accommodation – Kortdurende overbrugging Hoogspecialistische residentiële verblijfsvoorzieningen voor jeugdigen
description: Middels de onderhavige aanbestedingsprocedure beoogt SDF hoogspecialistische residentiële verblijfsvoorzieningen in te kopen. Het gaat hierbij om een hoogspecialistische verblijfsplek met behandelfocus, gericht op gedragsverandering en ontwikkeling. Er is 24uurs toezicht en intensieve begeleiding aanwezig. Er wordt een positief en passend pedagogisch opvoed- en behandelklimaat geboden. De dagelijkse opvoeding en begeleiding bij onderwijs en vrijetijdsbesteding staan hierin centraal. Vanuit de kleinschaligheid wordt stabiliteit, relationele veiligheid, nabijheid geboden op basis van de individuele begeleiding en behandelbehoefte van de jeugdige. Het accent van de begeleiding en behandeling ligt op traumasensitief en gezinsgericht werken. Het team biedt een veilige sfeer gericht op de basisbehoeften van de jeugdige vanuit de systeemgerichte benadering en een pedagogisch behandelklimaat. Behandeling en begeleiding wordt op maat ingezet en waar nodig wordt aanvullende specialistische expertise toegevoegd en volledig geïntegreerd in het behandel- en opvoedklimaat. Er is sprake van een integraal dagprogramma met onderwijs, dagbesteding en vrijetijdsbesteding en actieve betrokkenheid van ouders en het netwerk. Elke verblijfslocatie investeert actief in de samenwerking met het onderwijs. Professionals werken multidisciplinair samen, nemen samen met jeugdige en gezin besluiten en kijken verder dan het eigen vakgebied en werken nauw samen met de gemeentelijke lokale teams. Er wordt een integraal pakket geboden, waarbij er op basis van individuele behoefte van de jeugdige wordt gekeken naar wat er nodig is. Het aanbod hoogspecialistische residentiele verblijfsvoorzieningen betreft specifiek twee doelgroepen: Jeugdigen met zeer complexe gedrags- en emotieregulatieproblematiek waarvoor intensieve nabijheid en toezicht noodzakelijk is (ca. 28-32 plekken); Jeugdigen met een licht verstandelijke beperking plus (LVB+) i.c.m. (zeer) complexe problematiek, ernstige gedrags- en emotieregulatieproblemen, waarvoor intensieve nabijheid en toezicht noodzakelijk is (ca. 12 plekken). Om aan te sluiten bij de behoeften van beide doelgroepen, bestaat de opdracht uit twee afzonderlijke percelen. De opdrachtnemer kan voor maximaal één perceel een overeenkomst aangaan.

title: Review of Danish MFA Support to the Global Youth Programme of the Danish Youth Council (DUF)
description: BACKGROUND The assignment concerns a Review of Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) support to the Global Youth Programme (GYP) of the Danish Youth Council (DUF). The key objective of the GYP is to strengthen democratic youth organizations and to increase young people’s participation in, and influence on, their communities and society. The Review is part of the regular monitoring of the ongoing partnership between the Danish MFA and DUF, and will be led by the Department for Evaluation, Learning and Quality (LEARNING) of the Danish MFA. OBJECTIVE The objective of the MTR is to is to support the MFA Department for Evaluation, Learning and Quality (LEARNING) in assessing the overall performance in the implementation of the DUF-managed Global Youth Programme, including achievements, risks and challenges faced. Based on the findings, the MTR is expected to formulate recommendations to strengthen and adapt the initiative. SCOPE OF WORK AND METHOD While not an evaluation, the Review will be carried out in accordance with OECD/DAC evaluation criteria, with focus on relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency and sustainability. The scope of work will cover two levels: a) the programme level for a cross-cutting and more strategic perspective, and b) the project level examining a sample of individual member organisations and their projects – the sampling approach will be developed during the inception phase. OUTPUTS The Review Team is expected to provide the following outputs: (1) a Mission Preparation Note (MPN) of approx. 5 pages, excluding annexes; (2) a post-mission de-briefing presentation; (3) a draft Review Report, and (4) a final Review Report of max. 20 pages, excluding annexes. TEAM COMPOSITION/CONSULTANTS A team of two international consultants is required for this assignment. Expert 1 should be a specialist in Youth Engagement and Civil Society Organisations with extensive review experience. Expert 2 should be a specialist in financial management and civil society funding mechanisms, including pooled funds. One of the experts, preferably Expert 1, should be designated as coordinator for the team of consultants. Both experts are expected to participate in mission travel (see below), most likely to one or two African countries. Both experts must be fluent in English. The Review team will be led by a chief advisor from the MFA LEARNING department. TIMING The Review is expected to start 5 January 2027 (date TBC), and conclude in March 2027 (date TBC). A mission of maximum 10 days is expected in late-January/early-February (dates TBC). MAXIMUM BUDGET 500,000 DKK (net of VAT) Deadline for application: 6 November 2026 at 14:00 Danish time Interested Consultants can request to get the instructions prepared for applicants by e-mail to the Contact person stated below Contact point Department for Evaluation, Learning And Quality Contact person Nanna Kirkegaard on behalf of Pelle Lütken Contact e-mail laeringstud@um.dk Criteria for selection A minimum of three and a maximum of five applicants with references best suited for the assignment will be invited to submit a tender.

title: Conversion of Storm Shelter into Public Convenience Facilities and Refurbishment of Accessible Toilet Accommodation, Blenheim Gardens, Minehead
description: Minehead Town Council invites suitably qualified and experienced contractors to submit tenders for the conversion of the former storm shelter within Blenheim Gardens, Minehead into modern public convenience facilities together with the refurbishment and conversion of a separate toilet building within the gardens to provide fully accessible toilet accommodation and associated storage facilities. The site occupies a prominent position within Blenheim Gardens, Minehead's principal public open space, and lies within the Wellington Square Conservation Area. The Council wishes to deliver attractive, durable, accessible and vandal-resistant facilities whilst preserving the architectural character and appearance of the existing buildings. The works comprise the alteration, refurbishment and fit out of two existing buildings. The former storm shelter will be converted to provide male and female public toilet accommodation, baby changing facilities and associated handwashing facilities. A separate building within the gardens will be refurbished to provide a fully accessible toilet facility together with independent storage accommodation. The project includes, but is not limited to, demolition and alteration works, drainage works, utility connections, plumbing and sanitary installations, electrical installations, ventilation systems, roofing replacement and repairs, internal finishes, accessibility improvements, external repairs, testing, commissioning and all associated works necessary to provide fully operational public convenience facilities. The successful contractor will be responsible for providing all labour, materials, plant, supervision and specialist subcontractors required to complete the works. Responsibilities will include project management, utility provider liaison, Building Regulations compliance, testing, commissioning, certification and handover. Particular emphasis is placed upon durability, long-term maintainability, accessibility and resistance to vandalism. Materials, fixtures, fittings and finishes must be suitable for intensive public use and capable of withstanding a coastal environment exposed to wind-driven rain, salt-laden air and high seasonal visitor numbers. Tenderers shall demonstrate relevant experience in the successful delivery of comparable construction and refurbishment projects and provide evidence of their ability to meet programme requirements. The completed facilities must be fully operational and available for public use no later than 1 March 2027. The Council reserves the right not to accept the lowest or any tender received and reserves the right to amend, suspend, abandon or recommence the procurement process at any stage.

title: Peatland ACTION FW02 Field Ecologists Framework
description: NatureScot work to improve our natural environment in Scotland and inspire everyone to care more about it. We work to ensure that all nature in Scotland - our key habitats and landscapes, all our green space and our native species - are maintained, enhanced and bring us benefits. Our priority is a nature-rich future for Scotland and an effective response to the climate emergency. Peatland ACTION funding - from Scottish Government - primarily supports on-the-ground peatland restoration activities and is open for applications from eligible land managers who have peatlands that would benefit from restoration. There are no geographical restrictions or target areas for Peatland ACTION funding. Peatlands are an iconic part of the Scottish landscape and have many benefits for people and nature. Healthy peatlands provide important ecosystem services including storing and sequestering carbon, supporting unique and specialised biodiversity, improving downstream water quality, and regulating water flow to provide natural flood management. In contrast, damage to peatlands reduces or reverses these benefits. For example, degraded peatlands release stored carbon and are a major global source of greenhouse gas emissions. Peatland ACTION is led and funded by Scottish Government and delivered in partnership with NatureScot, Cairngorms National Park Authority, Loch Lomond & the Trossachs National Park Authority, Forestry and Land Scotland, and Scottish Water. Since 2012, Peatland ACTION has set over 66,000 hectares of degraded peatland on the road to recovery, but this effort needs to accelerate rapidly in the coming years to help address the twin crises of the climate emergency and biodiversity loss. The appointed Field Ecologists will work with the Peatland ACTION Technical Team and Project Officers located across Scotland to help support species and ecological survey requirements for Peatland ACTION restoration sites.

description: Aberdeenshire Council are inviting tenders for Stonehaven Promenade Improvement works. title: Peatland ACTION FW02 Field Ecologists Framework
description: NatureScot work to improve our natural environment in Scotland and inspire everyone to care more about it. We work to ensure that all nature in Scotland - our key habitats and landscapes, all our green space and our native species - are maintained, enhanced and bring us benefits. Our priority is a nature-rich future for Scotland and an effective response to the climate emergency. Peatland ACTION funding - from Scottish Government - primarily supports on-the-ground peatland restoration activities and is open for applications from eligible land managers who have peatlands that would benefit from restoration. There are no geographical restrictions or target areas for Peatland ACTION funding. Peatlands are an iconic part of the Scottish landscape and have many benefits for people and nature. Healthy peatlands provide important ecosystem services including storing and sequestering carbon, supporting unique and specialised biodiversity, improving downstream water quality, and regulating water flow to provide natural flood management. In contrast, damage to peatlands reduces or reverses these benefits. For example, degraded peatlands release stored carbon and are a major global source of greenhouse gas emissions. Peatland ACTION is led and funded by Scottish Government and delivered in partnership with NatureScot, Cairngorms National Park Authority, Loch Lomond & the Trossachs National Park Authority, Forestry and Land Scotland, and Scottish Water. Since 2012, Peatland ACTION has set over 66,000 hectares of degraded peatland on the road to recovery, but this effort needs to accelerate rapidly in the coming years to help address the twin crises of the climate emergency and biodiversity loss. The appointed Field Ecologists will work with the Peatland ACTION Technical Team and Project Officers located across Scotland to help support species and ecological survey requirements for Peatland ACTION restoration sites.
